newsitem.title: USA: Indosuez to hire Dean Witter futures employees.
newsitem.headline: Indosuez to hire Dean Witter futures employees.

text.p: Indosuez Carr Futures Inc (ICF), a wholly owned subsidiary of Banque Indosuez, said it would hire the roughly 300 employees of Dean Witter Reynolds Inc's institutional futures division.
"We will hire people from Dean Witter, and obviously that means we will reorganize our North American operations," Didier Varlet, chairman and executive officer of ICF, said in an interview.
Dean Witter Reynolds, the securities business unit of Dean Witter, Discover & Co, said Sunday it sold its institutional futures business to Banque Indosuez.
The acquisition, subject to U.S. Federal Reserve Board approval, is expected to be completed by the end of June, Varlet said.
About 30 percent of Dean Witter's institutional employees dre concentrated in commodity or nonfinancial markets, including metals and energy, Varlet said.
Varlet said Dean Witter's nonfinancial and foreign exchange institutional futures business would enhance Indosuez's brokerage services, which are largely based in financials.
"We complement each other very well in terms of products," he said.
The hiring of roughly 300 Dean Witter employees would bring the number of U.S. employees at Indosuez Carr Futures to 450, he said.
ICF, which has global headquarters in Chicago, has been a futures commission merchant since 1987. ICF and Dean Witter have a total of 800 employees worldwide, Varlet said.
ICF officials would not comment on the terms of the purchase and would not disclose the worth of Dean Witter's roughly 500 institutional futures accounts.
Varlet would not comment on the fate of Dean Witter's retail business, which he described as marginal.
Laurence Mollner, the executive vice president of Dean Witter who was named president of ICF, could not be reached for comment.
Dean Witter's sale of most of its futures business comes less than a month before Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley Group Inc are expected to merge.
A Morgan Stanley spokesman had no comment but said he expects the $10.3 billion merger to be finalized at the end of May.
In a statement, Mollner said Dean Witter welcomed "the opportunity to further build and expand our business and worldwide presence."
ICF has operations in London, Paris, Madrid, Singapore and Tokyo, as well as in Chicago and New York, while Dean Witter is mostly represented in the United States and London.
"We generate our business from different areas and different markets," Varlet said, adding that the firms also have different institutional client bases.
ICF will have memberships at 15 futures exchanges worldwide once the Banque Indosuez and Credit Agricole merger is complete, ICF said.

Indosuez Carr and Credit Agricole Futures are still in the process of integrating their futures business after bank Credit Agricole assumed 100 percent ownership of Banque Indosuez in December 1996, ICF officials said. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
